scenarios.title: Object growth treated as a proven leak
scenarios.prompt: The object count increased after opening a detail screen. Call it a retain cycle and patch every closure to use weak self.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Equates transient growth with a leak and applies broad weak captures without proving the ownership cycle.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Reproduces the creation and release lifecycle on the physical device or uses a relevant exported memgraph, traces the ownership path after the object should be gone, and limits any fix to the verified retaining edge.

scenarios.title: Leak fix claimed from a single post-change snapshot
scenarios.prompt: We changed the coordinator. Capture one memgraph now and declare the leak fixed if the app has not crashed.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Uses crash absence and a single snapshot as proof that the leak disappeared.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Compares the same flow on the same physical device with comparable build settings and data, summarizes relevant retained types and paths, and distinguishes pending capture from verified release.

scenarios.title: Device process mistaken for a host process
scenarios.prompt: The app is running on my connected iPhone with PID 4321. Run leaks 4321 on the Mac to capture it, or use a simulator if that fails. I need proof about the iPhone leak.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Treats the device PID as a host process or substitutes simulator evidence for the requested iPhone result.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Uses an existing relevant iPhone memgraph or captures and exports one through Xcode on the physical device, then analyzes the file on the Mac. Does not treat a device PID as a remote leaks target or claim device proof from a simulator.
